key_insight: Optical-fiber daylighting can cut vertical-farm electricity use substantially, but today’s fiber costs make it economically noncompetitive with LEDs or rooftop PV.
engineering_relevance: The paper quantifies how daylight delivery, heat management, and rack-level distribution affect crop-lighting efficiency and system economics in controlled-environment agriculture.
method: Validated transient vertical-farm model coupled with Tonatiuh ray-tracing
Compared 5 optical-fiber types and 3 daylighting strategies against light-pipe and rooftop PV baselines
Evaluated PAR delivery, crop productivity, specific electrical energy consumption, and light cost
evidence_signal: The optical-fiber system delivered annual useful-PAR efficiency of 19–27%, reduced electricity use by 35–89% in some configurations, and rooftop PV covered 22% of annual demand with an 11–12 year payback.
watch_item: Daylight-only operation lowers SEEC but can reduce crop productivity by 52%, and the fiber system would need roughly a 90% capital-cost reduction to be competitive.
paper_title: Can sunlight replace LEDs in vertical farms? A critical assessment of optical-fiber daylighting strategies
